name: EventNotificationComponentClientFacet_SyncNotifications
summary: The server hands the client a set of notifications. A 102-byte record with a 98-byte body: the shared two-u64 head, a prefix-varint count of TEN, ten (key, value) pairs of two u32 BE, then one strict boolean byte. The container is exact on the byte - 16 + 1 + 10*8 + 1 = 98 with two bytes to spare on the varint-width allowance - and both the writer and the reader state the same shape independently.
purpose: Synchronise the notification component's map to the client. This is the only server-to-client type left unnamed in the 1.365 corpus, and the only one of the fifteen that the server must both encode and account for at world entry.

created_when: the notification facet syncs its map to the client, at seq 0x09 of world entry
lifecycle.if_absent: the client receives no notification state. The capture sends it third, after registration and the response, so it is early in the entry sequence rather than event-driven

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 a4 32, i.e. type index 3236 = 0xca4. A server record carries the body at record offset 4 - the typed header is the first four bytes - so a 98-byte body makes a 102-byte record. The typed header's second byte is 0x32, not 0x02: this is a WIDE prefix varint (n=1, low=0x24, continuation 0x32), value 50<<6 | 36 = 3236, and it round-trips through javelin/varint.py.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: Measured a0 b4 5f fb d9 b3 26 4b = 0xa0b45ffbd9b3264b. First u64 of the shared message head: the sending facet's own local id, the event-notification client facet. It is NOT any other facet id the atlas has named - the social, chat, mount, player, time, traversal and voice ids are all different - so this is the ninth per-component id in the corpus, and it appears on this wire only.
fields.provenance: corpus-wide scan; the head's first u64 is named in msg.time-sync-to-client.json from FUN_1416c1c40

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Measured bf 85 31 4b bc 4a 95 1a = 0xbf85314bbc4a951a, the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id - the same value every other capture carries.
fields.provenance: already earned in msg.time-sync-to-client.json; re-measured here

fields.name: notifications
fields.note: The element count (measured 0x0a = 10, so one byte) followed by that many 8-byte elements: 0x10 + 1 + 80 = 0x61, where the tail byte starts. counted(...) carries its own prefix-varint, so the count is part of this one field and is not declared twice. The writer FUN_143025640 writes the list size with FUN_140877b10 and the deserializer FUN_143027250 reads it with FUN_14087b760; both refuse a count at or above 0x2000001, which is where the bound comes from rather than being invented.
fields.provenance: decompile: writer FUN_143025640 (FUN_140877b10 on container +0x18) and deserializer FUN_143027250 (FUN_14087b760), both on container +0x28; element card codec.event-notification-entry; capture: 0x9_T0xca4_R.bin body[0x10..0x61]

fields.name: tail_flag
fields.note: Measured 0x01, and it is the body's last byte: 0x61 + 1 = 0x62 = 98, leaving nothing over. The writer writes it as a strict non-zero test from object +0x20 and the CLIENT's reader reads one byte through FUN_1408787b0 and REFUSES anything at or above 2. The vocabulary's bool_byte models only the width and the non-zero test, not that rejection, so the generated codec accepts 0x02 as true while this note records that the client would refuse it. What the flag switches is unnamed - one sample, value 1.
fields.provenance: decompile: writer FUN_14319b2a0 and deserializer FUN_14319b310; capture: 0x9_T0xca4_R.bin body[0x61]

reader FUN_14319b310 mirrors it: FUN_14150e670() for the shared head, FUN_143027250 on +0x28, then one FUN_1408787b0 byte with a `< 2` check. FUN_143027250 reads a prefix-varint count and, per element, exactly two FUN_14087a3c0 u32 reads. Writer and reader therefore agree field for field

the family confirms the container independently: 0xca2 RequestSendNotificationWithReplacements uses the SAME node walk (FUN_1407d64f0) with a u32 key and a STRING in the value slot, so the key-then-member shape is shared across the EventNotification types while the value's type is per-message. 0xca1 and 0xca7 share the one-u32 reader FUN_1426d64f0, and 0xca8 shares the bool reader FUN_1425a3070
record 0x9_T0xca4_R.bin at seq 0x09, 102 bytes: typed header 00 01 a4 32, then body a0b45ffbd9b3264b | bf85314bbc4a951a | 0a | ten (key, value) u32 pairs | 01. 16 + 1 + 80 + 1 = 98 exactly

the 1.365 corpus supplies no second sample of 0xca4, so every field meaning beyond the container rests on this one record. The layout is nonetheless complete: both the writer and the separate reader account for all 98 bytes, and the element's key/value split comes from the map insert, not from the sample
